correctness.rationale: The stochastic generator is elliptic with a unique stationary state and a Poisson corrector. Perturbation gives H(t)=sum w(t-k²)/(t+k²)² by the invariant-density correction and martingale quadratic variation. At a new large odd wave number k and weight k^(3/2), each old finite witness changes by O(k^(-1/2)), the new witness t=k is negative because -k^(-1/2) dominates O(k^(-1)) old terms, and t=2k² is strictly positive. Induction and finite strict-sign continuity imply at least 2m-1 physical diffusion crossings for sufficiently small epsilon. Exact rational checks reproduce all four two-mode signs. Galerkin calculations corroborate but are not treated as proof.

originality.rationale: Established homogenization and first-passage equations cover the underlying flashing-potential models and methods, but their inspected source claims do not establish a smooth finite-Fourier construction with an unbounded number of alternating above/below-thermal diffusivity intervals. The new weak-amplitude kernel plus high-frequency sign-induction generates a qualitative phenomenon not implied by the published single-profile examples. The older close journal article was accessible as an abstract only; any unindexed direct equivalent would overturn priority, so the assessment is qualified.

value.rationale: Reentrant above/below-thermal diffusion windows are transport regimes that affect interpretation of flashing ratchets, not a routine optimization of an arbitrary coefficient. Explicit two-harmonic data demonstrate three changes, and the induction shows no model-wide finite crossing bound without a fixed spectral-support assumption. The result separates the geometry of a multiscale potential from the switching-rate scale and delimits simple single-profile conclusions. It is an exact fixed-model existence theorem, not a numerical survey.
